findings.text: the declarations map and §2's section element (plan.html:65) both read `s2: done`, but the plan's own `c-partial-r-20261107T162323087195` comment at plan.html:315, written the day before, states that only the first of the section's three nodes has landed and that "the second (small dispatch-time fields and peer_channel) and third (dispatch_options at launch, suite_evidence) remain, so the section stays implementable"; the record also names no landing evidence for those two nodes

findings.reason: an unstated margin and an unbounded exclusion leave the worker to invent the threshold, so the gate it builds is not the one the plan says counts as done.
findings.text: the launch clause is "a launch that would leave the node's scratch volume below a stated free margin is held as a placement wait", but the section states no margin (plan.html:222-225 give a 23 GB volume and its 17 GB occupancy, never a threshold), and the first clause's "no per-run scratch … beyond what its review and landing read" defines no quantity a test can assert, so two of the node's three measures have no tolerance to be judged against

findings.reason: with no reverted guard the placement-wait case can pass on a launch that never consults free space, so the node closes without showing its refusal fires.
findings.text: §13 declares no negative control, where §2, §3, §4, §5 and §6 each name one as a mutated guard that must fail (plan.html:109, 130, 141, 151, 172); "these still hold: a live run keeps its scratch, and settling never removes a directory whose run is live" restates invariants the new code must preserve rather than a mutation that reddens a case

findings.reason: one gate cannot show both guards fire, so a node that lands settling and leaves admission unbuilt closes as done on half its endpoint.
findings.text: the done-when joins two independent deliverables: a settling change so a delivered run's per-run scratch is gone, and an admission change so a launch whose node would fall below a free margin is held as a placement wait; they fail independently, live in different code paths (`reckon/crew/gc.py` versus `reckon/crew/placement.py` and the launch path) and the stated write scope names both plus `dispatch_launch.py`

findings.reason: without a named durable path the node's all_debug arms and its before/after volume readings survive only in a run directory §3 retires after a day's grace, so no later reader can check the claim the section was written for.
findings.text: §13's gate and base arms run on all_debug and its only host facts are measurements of the reservation node's volume, yet the section names no log directory, no evidence fragment and no committed record, unlike §8 and §11 which say "Every log is under the run directory" and cite a fragment; the 23 GB volume, 17 GB and 61-directory figures in the Why also carry no committed source

findings.reason: the node as written would reimplement a guard that already fires and rebuild a test that is green at base, leaving the actual cause of 17 GB on the reservation node — a scratch/state-root pairing refusal (`settle_run_scratch` returns "state and scratch roots differ"), copies whose run directories lack an exit record, or a backlog of live runs — undiscovered.
findings.text: the Why claims scratch is settled "only once a run is over" and that "a delivered run awaiting review or landing is not over, so a backlog of delivered runs … keeps its scratch", but §8's landed `settle_run_scratch` (`reckon/crew/gc.py:1672-1780`) settles on exactly three facts — no live pointer, no process holder, and `_run_directory_records_end` (`exit.json`/`discard.json`/`attempt-*-exit.json`, gc.py:1656-1670) — with no grace and no review state, and it is already called from every launch (dispatch_launch.py:928), from the step wrapper (dispatch_launch.py:1367) and from the retention sweep (gc.py:2266); so the stated cause names a review-state gate the code does not have, and the section's first clause would pass on the base revision, contradicting "New tests, each failing at the base revision"
